chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

He was asked about a woman who had a husband absent from her, so she married another husband. He said: If it was brought to the Imam, and witnesses testified against her that she had an absent husband, and that his provisions and news came to her from him, and that she had married another husband, then it was upon the Imam to lash her and separate her from the one she married. It was said to him: What is done with the dowry she took from him? He said: If he had intercourse with her, he takes it; and if he did not have intercourse with her, then all that she took from him is forbidden to her, like the wage of the prostitute.

key_terms.أَجْرِ الْفَاجِرَةِ: The wage of the prostitute, used here as a metaphor for the compensation due for temporary use without full marital rights.
key_terms.الْإِمَام: The Imam, the religious and political leader who has the authority to judge and execute rulings.
key_terms.الْمَهْر: The dowry or bridal gift given to the wife.
key_terms.يَحُدَّهَا: To lash or flog her as a legal punishment (hadd).
key_terms.يُفَرِّقَ: To separate or divorce, ending the marital bond.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's second marriage if her first husband is absent, and how is the dowry handled?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Isfabar highlights the Imam’s judicial discretion in resolving the conflict of concurrent marriages (ta'arud) when the first husband is absent, emphasizing the necessity of witness testimony regarding his provision to validate the first bond. The distinction in dowry retention based on consummation reflects the principle that the second marriage is valid but potentially defective (zawaj al-shubha), with the 'wage of the prostitute' metaphor underscoring the woman's liability for the period of uncertainty. This case illustrates the practical application of fiqh in managing social and legal complexities arising from prolonged absence in early Shia jurisprudence.
